notes.headline: JD.com: profit up 58% as food-delivery losses shrink and revenue returns to growth, but the shares fall 8% on weak momentum
notes.takeaway: Revenue rose 3.5% to RMB309.6 billion and non-GAAP earnings per ADS rose 58% to RMB5.88, exactly in line with forecasts, as losses in food delivery narrowed and marketing spend fell. JD closed its purchase of Germany’s Ceconomy, but with revenue growth barely positive, the ADRs dropped 7.7%.
results: JD.com reported net revenue of RMB309.6 billion (US$46.2 billion) for the third quarter, up 3.5%. Operating income was RMB5.2 billion, a margin of 1.7%, against a RMB1.1 billion loss a year earlier; non-GAAP operating income was RMB7.3 billion, a 2.4% margin. Non-GAAP net income rose to RMB8.3 billion from RMB5.8 billion, and non-GAAP diluted earnings per ADS rose 57.6% to RMB5.88 (US$0.88), matching the consensus.

JD Retail, the core e-commerce business, earned RMB15.1 billion of operating income, a 5.8% margin, against RMB14.8 billion and 5.9% a year earlier. New Businesses — mainly JD Food Delivery, the discount platform Jingxi and the international operations — reduced their losses both year on year and from the second quarter.

Free cash flow on the company’s measure was negative for the quarter after higher capital spending and working-capital movements. Net income attributable to shareholders under GAAP was RMB6.5 billion, against RMB5.3 billion.
mgmt: Chief executive Sandy Xu said JD returned to positive revenue growth while accelerating profit growth, underpinned by the resilience of JD Retail and continued loss reduction in New Businesses, and that the user base expanded alongside a notable reduction in marketing expenses. She described the closing of the Ceconomy acquisition, the owner of MediaMarkt and Saturn, as an important step in JD’s globalisation.

Chief financial officer Ian Su Shan said JD Retail kept its margin largely stable against a high base and that the Joybuy international platform is building momentum, which synergies with Ceconomy should strengthen. The company also launched an AI shopping assistant, Dongdong, with version 16.0 of its app.
view: JD spent 2025 in a costly war with Meituan and Alibaba over instant food delivery, a market it entered largely to defend its users’ shopping frequency. That fight crushed profit a year ago; this quarter shows the losses shrinking quickly, which is why non-GAAP earnings rose 58%. The improvement is real, but it is the recovery from a self-inflicted wound rather than new earning power, and the market knows the difference.

The core problem is growth. Revenue up 3.5% for China’s largest direct retailer reflects soft Chinese demand for electronics and appliances, its largest categories, and JD Retail’s margin is now essentially flat. The Ceconomy deal is the answer management is offering — a ready-made European retail network of more than 1,000 stores to sell Chinese-made electronics and support Joybuy — but it brings a low-margin, mature business with its own restructuring challenges.

That leaves JD valued as a low-growth, low-margin retailer at around 15 times trailing earnings, with a large cash pile and a buyback programme cushioning the downside. The shares will rerate only if either Chinese consumption recovers or the international strategy proves it can earn more than European retail typically does. Neither showed up in this quarter, which explains why a 58% earnings increase still produced a falling share price.
notes.watch: Watch JD Retail revenue growth in the fourth-quarter shopping season, the remaining losses in food delivery, the first quarter of consolidated Ceconomy results, and the pace of share buybacks.
